summary: Nez Perce L-5 log cabin built 1930 on a 1922 site; staffed into the 1960s, now emergency use, reached by a seasonal 4WD road.

facts.status_note: Found in good condition on a fall 2020 visit, but the Forest Service page calls the spot the site of the historic lookout.

staffing.status: not staffed since the 1960s; emergency use

access.note: Forest Service recreation site, open seasonally due to snow. Reached by Forest Road 468-C, recommended for 4WD only. The cabin is maintained for emergency use.

visit.trail_note: Road 468-C is unmaintained and rocky, 4WD recommended, seasonal. No restrooms or potable water. Trail 539 nearby reaches McArthur, Stillman and Burnt Knob lakes.

events.note: Ranger station established on the Shoup Trail; the lookout point is one-quarter mile from it.
Elmer Purdyman listed by Idaho Fire Lookouts from a 1915 Idaho County Free Press item. Predates both the alidade and the cabin.
Site first used, with an alidade placed on the summit.
L-5 log lookout cabin built on the granite ridge.
Idaho Fire Lookouts dates emergency status to 1964. NHLR says staffed until the 1960s; firelookout.com says used until the early 1960s.
Restoration work by district employees; dated only to the late 1980s (firelookout.com says 'late 1980').
Fall 2020 visit, reported by Idaho Fire Lookouts, found the cabin in good condition despite smoke.

corrections.why: The NHLR and Forest Service pages use Burnt Knob Lookout. The extra alias is a misspelling and should not be listed as another name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 8,011 ft (2,442 m), matching the record's 2441.8 m. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 8,196 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
NHLR says staffed until the 1960s, firelookout.com says used until the early 1960s, and Idaho Fire Lookouts says emergency status began in 1964. The story reports the range and the 1964 date.

NHLR says maintained for emergency use. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags it Drive-Up Abandoned. The Forest Service page (last updated February 18, 2026) calls it an open seasonal site and the site of the historic lookout. The story gives all three and uses the Forest Service page for current access.

notes_for_editor: Rental status is not confirmed. A reader comment on the Idaho Fire Lookouts post points to recreation.gov, but no listing was read, so the story says nothing about rental. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Drive-Up Abandoned tag is its own category and is not treated as a current status. Photos not added, though University of Idaho Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness History Project items (sbw019, sbw087; 1938 photographs) surfaced in search and could be checked for license and use. The 1930 cabin date is consistent across three sources.
